glasgow_merchant_guide.text: Welcome to the Merchant City. In the 1700s the Tobacco Lords built their grand townhouses and warehouses on these streets.
By the 1760s Glasgow was Britain's biggest tobacco port. Ships sailed from the Clyde to Virginia and Maryland, and the Clyde is a handy bit closer to America than London.
That fortune rested on tobacco grown by enslaved people. Buchanan, Glassford and Ingram Streets are named for tobacco merchants. Glasgow talks about that openly now.

glasgow_merchant_volunteer.text: Up the road, the Duke of Wellington statue wears a traffic cone. The council once planned to raise the plinth to stop it. Glaswegians took that as a challenge, and the plan was dropped.
